title: RC-Mixup: A Data Augmentation Strategy against Noisy Data for Regression Tasks

problem.claim: Robust data augmentation is needed for regression tasks when the data contains noise.

gap.claim: C-Mixup does not distinguish noisy from clean samples, which can cause problematic mixing and suboptimal model performance.

contributions.claim: RC-Mixup integrates C-Mixup with multi-round robust training methods.
RC-Mixup uses the interaction between C-Mixup and robust training so that C-Mixup helps identify clean data while robust training supplies cleaner data for mixing.
RC-Mixup is data-centric and does not require modifying the robust model training algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In experiments, RC-Mixup significantly outperforms C-Mixup and robust training baselines on noisy-data benchmarks.
The authors report that RC-Mixup can be integrated with various robust training methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies robust data augmentation for noisy regression tasks.
Existing Mixup methods primarily target classification, while C-Mixup adapts mixing to regression using label distances.
C-Mixup does not distinguish noisy and clean samples, creating a risk of harmful mixing and reduced performance.
RC-Mixup combines C-Mixup with multi-round robust training, allowing each component to improve the other's handling of clean data.
The authors report data-centric integration, improved benchmark performance, and compatibility with multiple robust training methods.

source_observation.claim: C-Mixup selects samples using label distances but does not distinguish noisy from clean samples.

interpretation.claim: Selection criteria that improve task alignment may still be insufficient when data quality varies across samples.

application.claim: For noisy regression augmentation, combine task-aware sample mixing with a mechanism that identifies or supplies cleaner samples.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson applies beyond regression tasks or the reported noisy-data benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: RC-Mixup leaves the robust model training algorithm unchanged and adds data mixing.

interpretation.claim: Data-centric augmentation can improve a training pipeline while preserving the underlying robust-training algorithm.

application.claim: When extending existing robust-training methods, first evaluate whether augmentation can provide gains without modifying the core optimizer or training procedure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which robust training methods support integration or the conditions under which integration succeeds.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the noise models, datasets, benchmark composition, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe the RC-Mixup algorithm, mixing procedure, or multi-round training schedule.
The abstract does not quantify the reported performance improvements.
The abstract does not identify the robust training methods used for integration.
